This AI Can Help You Pass Your Exams Without Reading Everything?

Exams are approaching, your lecture notes are piling up, and there never seems to be enough time. Can AI help you study less but understand more? Here is how students can use AI tools to revise smarter without skipping the important work.

By LokkeeVerse · 7 min read

Imagine Preparing for an Exam Without Reading Every Page

Imagine you have five courses to prepare for, hundreds of pages of lecture notes, and only a few days before your exams begin.

For many Nigerian university students, this situation is familiar. You may have missed a lecture, struggled to understand a topic, or waited until the examination timetable was released before taking revision seriously.

But what if you could use artificial intelligence to turn your lecture notes into summaries, generate practice questions, and explain complicated topics in simpler language?

AI tools can help you do these things. However, the trick is knowing how to use them without relying on answers that might be incorrect or missing important details.

1. Turn Long Lecture Notes Into Short Summaries

One of the biggest challenges students face is the amount of material they need to cover before an exam.

Instead of asking AI to summarize an entire course into a few sentences, upload or paste your lecture notes and ask it to identify the major concepts, definitions, examples, and likely areas to revise.

You can try this prompt:

"Act as my university exam tutor. Summarize these lecture notes into clear revision notes. Keep all important definitions, concepts, examples, formulas, and explanations. Organize the content by topic and highlight areas I should understand before my exam. Do not remove important information just to make the summary shorter."

This can help you get through lengthy materials more efficiently while keeping the main ideas organized.

Remember to compare the summary with your original notes to make sure important details have not been left out.

2. Ask AI to Explain What Your Lecturer Taught

Sometimes, the problem is not the length of the notes. It is understanding what they mean.

You might read the same paragraph several times without understanding it. An AI tutor can explain the topic using simpler language, examples, and step-by-step explanations.

For example, a computer science student struggling with database normalization could ask:

"Explain database normalization to me as if I am a beginner. Use simple examples, explain the different normal forms step by step, and give me one practice question after each explanation."

You can use the same approach for accounting, economics, biology, mathematics, law, and other subjects.

If the explanation is still confusing, ask the AI to explain it differently rather than memorizing something you do not understand.

3. Generate Practice Questions From Your Notes

Reading your notes can make you feel prepared even when you cannot remember the information without looking at the page.

That is why practising questions is important.

AI tools can turn your lecture materials into multiple-choice questions, short-answer questions, definitions, and essay questions.

Try this prompt:

"Using only the lecture notes I provide, generate 20 university-level exam practice questions. Include multiple-choice questions, short-answer questions, and essay questions. Do not show the answers until I attempt the questions. After I answer, mark my responses, explain my mistakes, and identify the topics I need to revise."

This method helps you discover what you actually understand and what you still need to study.

AI-generated questions are practice materials, not guaranteed predictions of what your lecturer will ask in the examination.

4. Use AI to Understand Past Questions

Past questions can help you understand how your lecturer sets examinations and how topics are tested.

If you have past questions, provide them alongside your course outline or lecture notes. Ask AI to explain what each question requires and guide you through the solution.

For example:

"Help me prepare for this course using these past questions and lecture notes. Group the questions by topic, explain how to approach each type of question, and create similar practice questions. Do not claim that a topic will appear in my next exam unless there is evidence for that conclusion."

This can be especially useful when you struggle to understand what an exam question is asking.

However, do not study only the questions you already have. Your upcoming examination may cover different topics or use different question formats.

5. Try These AI Tools for Exam Preparation

Here are three options worth exploring.

ChatGPT

ChatGPT can explain difficult concepts, quiz you, create flashcards, and help you work through problems step by step. Its Study Mode is designed to guide learning through explanations and questions rather than simply giving quick answers.

You can explore it at https://chatgpt.com/studymode.

NotebookLM

NotebookLM is useful when you want to study from your own materials. You can upload supported course documents and ask questions about them, create study guides, and generate quizzes or flashcards based on your sources.

Visit https://notebooklm.google.com.

Gemini

Gemini can help explain concepts, summarize information, and support revision. Google's study notebook features can also help organize learning materials and create personalized study activities where available.

Visit https://gemini.google.com.

Features and access limits can vary, so check what is available on your account before relying on a particular tool.

6. A Simple AI Revision Plan for Nigerian Students

Suppose you have three days before an examination. You could organize your revision like this:

Day 1: Collect your lecture notes and course outline. Use AI to organize the material into topics, summarize difficult sections, and identify what you do not understand.

Day 2: Study the topics that need the most attention. Ask AI to explain them, then answer practice questions without looking at your notes.

Day 3: Attempt past questions under timed conditions. Review your mistakes, revisit weak topics, and confirm important facts and definitions using your lecturer's materials.

Adjust this plan to your course, exam format, and the time you have available. A difficult technical course may require more practice than a course focused mainly on definitions and essays.

7. The Biggest Mistake Students Make With AI

The biggest mistake is allowing AI to do all the thinking.

If you ask AI for answers, read them once, and move on, you may recognize the information without being able to explain it during the exam.

Another risk is that AI can produce incorrect facts, misleading explanations, or answers that do not match your lecturer's preferred approach.

To avoid this, verify important information against your lecture notes, prescribed textbooks, course materials, and reliable sources. For calculations and technical subjects, practise solving problems yourself.

Also, follow your institution's rules about AI use, especially for assignments and assessments.

So, Can AI Help You Pass Without Reading Everything?

Yes, AI can help you prepare more efficiently, but it cannot guarantee that you will pass an examination.

You may not need to read every page with equal attention. You can use AI to organize notes, identify difficult topics, generate practice questions, and focus your revision where it matters most.

But you still need to understand the material, practise answering questions, and check that the information is correct.

The smarter approach is not to stop studying. It is to spend less time struggling with disorganized notes and more time understanding, remembering, and applying what you have learned.

**Try this today:** Pick one topic from your next examination, give your lecture notes to an AI study tool, and ask it to explain the topic before testing you with ten questions. See which questions you can answer without looking at your notes.
